## Evidence audit and scope

### 14.2 Examiner-report triangulation

Past examiner reports are used to identify **what candidates actually failed to demonstrate**, not to dictate the teaching sequence or replace full syllabus coverage.

| **Historical examination topic** | **Teaching implication incorporated** |
|---|---|
| 2021.1 and 2016.2: **recognition and immediate management of malignant hyperthermia** | Early ETCO₂ rise, prompt trigger cessation, immediate actual-weight dantrolene dosing/repetition, potassium/acidosis/cooling, team roles and ICU recurrence surveillance (Ch 3) |
| 2021.2: **75% TBSA major burn at district hospital prior to transfer** | Burn size and shock physiology, worked modified Parkland fluid rate, progressive airway oedema, inhalational poisons, dressing/temperature and retrieval readiness (Chs 1–2; case 1) |
| 2018.1: **child rescued from house fire** | Child-specific Lund–Browder sizing, maintenance fluids, airway review, co-oximetry, safeguarding and other trauma (Chs 1–2) |
| 2017.1: **HBOT indications and problems of providing treatment** | Mechanisms, emergency/elective indications, contraindications, pressure-related hazards, chamber-critical-care constraints and retrieval decisions (Ch 9) |
| **2026.1: adult core temperature 27°C**, AT_RT 1.17; reported pass rate 52.6% | Examiner specifically criticised unreflective generic trauma/ALS lists without hypothermia-specific management. Detailed circulatory assessment, gentle handling, modified drugs/defibrillation and ECLS selection are explicitly taught (Ch 5; case 4). |

The source workbook contains further historical SAQ tags, some of which are based on older reports not among the files supplied here. Where an exact historic stem/commentary has not been independently checked, it is treated as a **workbook mapping clue**, not as independently verified official examiner advice. The detailed original examiner text remains the primary source where accessible.

### 14.3 Evidence hierarchy, important controversies and audit decisions

**Most authoritative local practice requirements:** NZ National Burn Service 2025 (resuscitation/timing), MHANZ and ANZCA PS55 2026 (dantrolene preparation/stocks), ANZCOR July 2026 (hypothermia ALS), and ACEM/ANZCA/CICM PG52 2025 (transfer). These are applied directly in the management sections. [1,5,6,10,18]

**BJA Education teaching depth:** Major burns Part 1 (pathophysiology/initial airway/assessment) and Part 2 (anaesthesia, fluid creep, ICU, surgery and analgesia); MH susceptibility/trigger-free anaesthesia. These help explain why the guidelines require the actions they do. [3,4,8]

**Blue Book review:** The 2025 chapter **“Pulse oximetry – understanding the device and the sources of error”** explicitly discusses how COHb gives a falsely reassuring SpO₂ and the limits of dual-wavelength technology; this is integrated into Ch 2. The 2023 chapter **“Principles of visual design in cognitive aid development”** provides supporting context for crisis checklists but is not used as a substitute for the MH algorithm. The Blue Book editions were screened for direct topic relevance; these are the directly applicable contributions identified. [20,21]

**Treatment uncertainty is identified instead of hidden:** HBOT for CO poisoning has heterogeneous outcomes evidence; unlike DCS and arterial gas embolism, **routine HBOT for every COHb elevation is not recommended**. Dantrolene and MH treatment are supported by pathophysiology and consensus rather than a randomised untreated comparator trial. Antivenom use is toxin-specific with limited high-quality RCT evidence; never universalise a single dose across Australian snake species. Toxin-specific extracorporeal removal follows EXTRIP rather than a blanket “dialyse severe overdose” rule. HBOT for necrotising infection is an adjunct when supported by the relevant centre, never a reason to delay debridement.

**Practical clinical limitations:** The document does not replace a supervised airway, burns escharotomy, hyperbaric chamber or aeromedical competency assessment. Some antivenom brands, toxicology infusion regimens, ECLS criteria and local disaster activation numbers depend on institution and must be verified at the point of care. A standalone written audit can show intellectual coverage, not guarantee examination performance under time pressure.

### 14.4 Depth-audit decisions and limits

The independent post-draft audit compared all sixteen workbook rows (twelve COMPLETE THIS SET and four COMPONENT THIS SET) against the actual written explanations—not merely the location column of the existing crosswalk. All assigned topics now have focused physiological teaching, recognition, investigations, management and escalation content. Specific deficiencies corrected were burn-centre fluid-protocol provenance; post-burn airway and analgesia decision-making; operative burn haemorrhage and hyperkalaemia; detailed MH crisis operations; differentiated venous versus arterial gas embolism; post-rewarming ICU surveillance; ventilation-centred drowning ALS; Australian envenomation and electrical-injury monitoring; major toxicology indications for alkalinisation/dialysis; altitude-drug decisions; measurable PG52 oxygen reserves; botulism/tetanus ICU care; and disaster command/triage workflows.

Examiner triangulation included the 2019.2 burns viva (65% TBSA, airway injury, haemofiltration and operative blood loss), the 2021.2 severe-burn transfer SAQ, the 2021.1 malignant-hyperthermia SAQ, the 2026.1 severe-hypothermia SAQ and the 2026.1 unstable intra-hospital transfer scenario. The teaching now addresses the actual clinical distinctions highlighted in those reports. No one document can encompass every future viva variant, and four parent outcomes explicitly remain shared with other sets; this audit certifies their assigned Set 8 components, not unrelated components elsewhere.

Clinical uncertainty is deliberately retained where practice varies: adult burn formula coefficients (NZ 3 mL/kg/%TBSA starting protocol versus some lower-start international pathways); benefits of HBOT for selected CO poisoning; selection and amount of species-specific antivenom; adjunctive drug treatment for NMS; gas-embolism positioning; and the indications for specialised ECLS. Sources are guidelines or consensus where trials are lacking. Local burn, poison, retrieval, hyperbaric and MH services should direct real-patient treatment, with examination answers demonstrating the physiology and reasoning behind the choice.

## Core references and further reading

The following are the main sources **actually used or independently checked** for Set 8, with links. These are ordered by their role in the teaching, not by citation count. Textbook-style narrative is intentionally original synthesis rather than close reproduction of articles.

- **1.** **National Burn Centre / Health NZ (clinical guideline last reviewed September 2023).** [Initial Assessment & Management of Burn Injuries](https://www.tewhatuora.govt.nz/assets/For-health-professionals/Hospital-and-specialist-services/National-burn-service/nbs-initial-assessment-management-burn-injuries-guidelines.pdf). Primary NZ pathway, modified Parkland **3 mL/kg/%TBSA**, paediatric maintenance, burn referral and transfer.
- **2.** **NSW Agency for Clinical Innovation (2026).** [Burn fluid resuscitation](https://aci.health.nsw.gov.au/networks/burn-injury/resources/patient-management/fluid-resuscitation). Independent contemporary Australian comparison of resuscitation targets.
- **3.** **McCann C, Watson A, Barnes D (2022).** [Major burns: Part 1. Epidemiology, pathophysiology and initial management. BJA Education](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8847805/). Zones of injury, size/depth, inhalation risk, initial resuscitation.
- **4.** **McGovern C, Puxty K, Paton L (2022).** [Major burns: Part 2. Anaesthesia, intensive care and pain management. BJA Education](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9073309/). Operative bleeding, nutrition, thermal management, analgesia, fluid creep.
- **5.** **ANZCA (29 April 2026).** [PS55 MH update: Increased minimum recommended dantrolene stocks](https://www.anzca.edu.au/news-and-safety-alerts/ps55-mh-update-increased-minimum-recommended-dantrolene-stocks). Actual-body-weight dosing and 720 mg immediate/480 mg within an hour stocks.
- **6.** **Malignant Hyperthermia Australia & New Zealand (MHANZ, updated 2025/2026).** [Malignant Hyperthermia Resource Kit](https://malignanthyperthermia.org.au/sites/default/files/2026-03/MALIGNANT-HYPERTHERMIA-RESOURCE-KIT-2025%20V3%2014.1.26.pdf). Crisis algorithm, rapid dantrolene reconstitution and team actions.
- **7.** **Glahn KPE et al., European Malignant Hyperthermia Group (2025 publication).** [Recognition and management of an MH crisis: 2024 guideline update. British Journal of Anaesthesia](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39482150/). International MH management consensus.
- **8.** **Gupta PK, Bilmen JG, Hopkins PM (2021).** [Anaesthetic management of a known or suspected MH-susceptible patient. BJA Education](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8134759/). Non-triggering anaesthesia, workstation preparation and family assessment.
- **9.** **Wijdicks EFM, Ropper AH (2024).** [Neuroleptic Malignant Syndrome. New England Journal of Medicine](https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMra2404606). Clinical differential and NMS ICU management.
- **10.** **ANZCOR (2026).** [Guideline 11.10: Resuscitation in Special Circumstances](https://www.anzcor.org/home/adult-advanced-life-support/guideline-11-10-resuscitation-in-special-circumstances). Temperature staging, shocks/adrenaline alterations, ECLS pathways.
- **11.** **Resuscitation Council UK (2025).** [Special circumstances guidelines: accidental hypothermia and drowning](https://www.resus.org.uk/professional-library/2025-resuscitation-guidelines/special-circumstances-guidelines). Ventilation-first drowning and hypothermia comparisons.
- **12.** **Moon RE, Mitchell SJ (2025).** [Hyperbaric treatment of air or gas embolism: Current recommendations. Undersea & Hyperbaric Medicine](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/40249721/). Arterial and venous gas embolism and recompression.
- **13.** **Systematic review (2024).** [Venous air embolism: A systematic review](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2949788424000030). Clinical contexts, diagnosis and management uncertainties.
- **14.** **ANZCOR.** [First aid management of Australian snake bite](https://www.anzcor.org/home/first-aid/guideline-9-4-1-first-aid-management-of-australian-snake-bite). Pressure immobilisation, stillness and CPR.
- **15.** **Queensland Poisons Information Centre (April 2026).** [Polyvalent antivenom guidance](https://www.poisonsinfo.health.qld.gov.au/for-health-professionals/antidote-stocking-recommendations/antivenom-polyvalent). Contemporary species-specific use and precautions.
- **16.** **bpacnz (October 2026).** [Managing caustic exposures in primary care](https://bpac.org.nz/2026/caustics.aspx). HF toxic effects, calcium treatment and NZ National Poisons Centre advice.
- **17.** **Royal Children’s Hospital Melbourne.** [Hydrofluoric acid exposure](https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Hydrofluoric_Acid_Exposure/). Practical topical/systemic calcium strategies and contraindications.
- **18.** **ACEM/ANZCA/CICM (2025).** [PG52 Guideline for transport of critically ill patients](https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/a4542b62-9b7c-4e0d-91ed-03baa3b11d87/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/PG52-Guideline-for-transport-of-critically-ill-patients-2024-%28PILOT%29.PDF). Transport systems, personnel, equipment reserves, platform hazards and handover.
- **19.** **Wilderness Medical Society (2024 update).** [Prevention, diagnosis and treatment of acute altitude illness](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.wem.2023.05.013). AMS/HACE/HAPE treatment and dose tables.
- **20.** **Ruberry R (2025).** “Pulse oximetry – understanding the device and the sources of error.” In Australasian Anaesthesia 2025. [ANZCA Blue Book 2025](https://airr.anzca.edu.au/anzcacrisjspui/handle/11055/1305). Specifically documents the COHb–SpO₂ measurement failure.
- **21.** **Moi D, Maulder J, Zeloof D, Iyer D (2023).** “Principles of visual design in cognitive aid development.” In Australasian Anaesthesia 2023. [ANZCA Blue Book 2023](https://www.anzca.edu.au/getContentAsset/f1a580a9-36db-4c77-aa46-37d9f7e88f0b/80feb437-d24d-46b8-a858-4a2a28b9b970/Blue_Book_COMBINED_DIGITAL_v2.pdf?language=en). Useful for MH/disaster cognitive aids.
- **22.** **EXTRIP Workgroup.** [Recommendations for extracorporeal treatments in poisoning](https://www.extrip-workgroup.org/recommendations). Toxin-specific dialysis indications, including salicylates and lithium.
- **23.** **AHA/ILCOR (2025).** [Highlights of the 2025 Guidelines for CPR and ECC](https://www.heart.org/en/-/media/CPR-Files/2025-documents-for-cpr-heart-edits-posting/Resuscitation-Science/252500_Hghlghts_2025ECCGuidelines.pdf). General ventilation/resuscitation context alongside ANZCOR.
- **24.** **ANZCA Final Examination reports, supplied PDFs**: [ANZCA examinations](https://www.anzca.edu.au/education-training/anaesthesia-training-program/examinations). Exam-specific cross-checks, including 2026.1 severe hypothermia; the user-supplied report copies contain the applicable examiner commentary.
- **25.** **ANZCA Training Program Curriculum, December 2025 (v1.14)** (supplied local PDF). Exact parent outcome wording and curriculum context, reconciled with the learner’s 36-set workbook.
